# PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE] Contents of this Part

## Scope of this Part

## 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (a)the automatic transfer of some defended cases in the High Court;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (b)the circumstances in which defended cases may be sent from one County Court hearing centre or court office to another; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (c)the allocation of defended cases to case management tracks and, where applicable, their assignment to a complexity band. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (2) There are four tracks—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (a)the small claims track;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (b)the fast track;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (c)the intermediate track; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (d)the multi-track. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.1 .—(1) This Part provides for—] (Rule 26.9 sets out the normal scope of each track. Part 27 makes provision for the small claims track. Part 28 makes provision for the fast track and the intermediate track. Part 29 makes provision for the multi-track.)

## Automatic transfer in the High Court

## 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (a)the claim is for a specified amount of money;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (b)the claim was commenced in a court which is not the defendant’s home court;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (c)the claim has not been transferred to another defendant’s home court; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (d)the defendant is an individual. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (2) This rule does not apply where the claim was commenced in a specialist list. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (3) Where this rule applies, the court shall transfer the proceedings to the defendant’s home court when a defence is filed, unless paragraph (4) applies. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (Rule 2.3 defines ‘defendant’s home court’.)

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (4) Where the claimant notifies the court under rule 15.10 that they wish the proceedings to continue, the court shall transfer the proceedings to the defendant’s home court when it receives that notification from the claimant. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (Rule 15.10 deals with a claimant’s notice where the defence is that money claimed has been paid)

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (5) Where—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (a)the claim is against two or more defendants with different home courts; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (b)the defendant whose defence is filed first is an individual,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] proceedings are to be transferred under this rule to the home court of that defendant. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (6) The time when a claim is automatically transferred under this rule may be varied by a practice direction in respect of claims issued by the Production Centre. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.2. —(1) This rule applies to proceedings in the High Court where—] (Rule 7.10 makes provision for the Production Centre.)

## Transfer of money claims within the County Court

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] 26.3. —(1) This rule applies where the claim is for an amount of money in the County Court, specified or unspecified. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (2) If at any time a court officer considers that the claim should be referred to a judge for directions, the court officer may send the proceedings to the defendant’s home court or the preferred hearing centre or other County Court hearing centre as may be appropriate. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (3) Subject to paragraphs (5) and (6), if the defendant is an individual and the claim is for a specified sum of money, at the relevant time the claim must be sent to the defendant’s home court (save that where there are two or more defendants, one or more of whom are individuals, the claim must be sent to the home court of the defendant who first files their defence). [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (4) Subject to paragraphs (5) and (6), in any other claim to which this rule applies, the court must, at the relevant time, send the claim to the preferred hearing centre. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (5) Subject to paragraph (6), if, on their directions questionnaire—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (a)a defendant under paragraph (3) has specified a hearing centre other than the defendant’s home court; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (b)a claimant under paragraph (4) has specified a hearing centre other than the preferred hearing centre,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] the claim must be sent to that other hearing centre. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (6) At the relevant time, the claim must be sent to the County Court at Central London if—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (a)the claim is started at the Civil National Business Centre;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (b)a court officer provisionally decides, pursuant to rule 26.4, that the track which appears to be most suitable for the claim is the multi-track; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (c)either—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (i)in respect of a defendant under paragraphs (3) and (5)(a), the home court (or the home court of the defendant who first files their defence) or the hearing centre specified on the directions questionnaire; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (ii)in respect of a claimant under paragraphs (4) and (5)(b), the preferred hearing centre or the hearing centre specified on the directions questionnaire,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] is one of the hearing centres listed in Practice Direction 26 at paragraph 19. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (7) The relevant time for the purposes of this rule is when—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (a)all parties have filed their directions questionnaires;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (b)any stay ordered by the court or period to attempt settlement through mediation has expired; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (c)if the claim falls within Practice Direction 49D—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (i)the defence is filed; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] (ii)enforcement of a default judgment other than by a warrant of control is requested,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Transfer of money claims within the County Court] whichever occurs first. ## Directions questionnaire

## 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (a)a court officer shall—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (i)provisionally decide the track which appears to be most suitable for the claim; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (ii)serve on each party a notice of proposed allocation; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (b)the notice of proposed allocation shall—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (i)specify any matter to be complied with by the date specified in the notice;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (ii)require the parties to file a completed directions questionnaire and serve copies on all other parties;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (iii)state the address of the court or the court office to which the directions questionnaire must be returned;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (iv)inform the parties how to obtain the directions questionnaire; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (v)if a case appears suitable for allocation to the fast track, intermediate track or multi-track, require the parties to file proposed directions by the date specified in the notice. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (2) The court shall serve on any unrepresented party the appropriate directions questionnaire. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (3) Where there are two or more defendants and at least one of them files a defence, the court shall serve the notice under paragraph (1)—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (a)when all the defendants have filed a defence; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (b)when the period for the filing of the last defence has expired,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] whichever is the sooner. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (Rule 15.4 specifies the period for filing a defence.)

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (4) If proceedings are automatically transferred under rule 26.2 or rule 26.3 the court in which the proceedings have been commenced—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (a)shall serve the notice of proposed allocation before the proceedings are transferred; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (b)shall not transfer the proceedings until all parties have complied with the notice or the time for doing so has expired. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (5) If rule 15.10 applies, the court shall not serve a notice under rule 26.4(1) until the claimant has filed a notice requiring the proceedings to continue. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (6) If a notice is served under paragraph (1)—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (a)each party must file, and serve on all other parties, the documents required by the notice by no later than the date specified in it; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (b)the date specified must be—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (i)if the notice relates to the small claims track, at least 14 days; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (ii)if the notice relates to the fast track, intermediate track, or multi-track, at least 28 days,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] after the date when it is deemed to be served on the party in question. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (7) The date for complying with a notice served under paragraph (1) may not be varied by agreement between the parties. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (8) The time when the court serves a directions questionnaire under this rule may be varied by a practice direction in respect of claims issued by the Production Centre. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (9) If a claim is a claim to which rule 26.3 applies and a party does not comply with the notice served under paragraph (1) by the date specified—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (a)the court shall serve a further notice on that party, requiring them to comply within 7 days; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (b)if that party fails to comply with the notice served under sub-paragraph (a), the party’s statement of case shall be struck out without further order of the court. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (10) If a claim is a claim to which rule 26.2 applies and a party does not comply with the notice served under paragraph (1) by the date specified, the court may make such order as it considers appropriate, including—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (a)an order for directions;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (b)an order striking out the claim;

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (c)an order striking out the defence and entering judgment; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (d)listing the case for a case management conference. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (11) Where a case has been struck out under paragraph (9)(b) or an order has been made under paragraph (10), a party who was in default shall, unless the court thinks it unjust to do so, be ordered to pay the costs that the default caused to any other party. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (Rule 7.10 makes provision for the Production Centre.)

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.4. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, if a defendant files a defence—] (Rules 6.14 and 6.26 specify when a document is deemed to be served.)

## Stay to allow for settlement of the case

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Stay to allow for settlement of the case] 26.5. —(1) A party may, when filing the completed directions questionnaire, make a written request for the proceedings to be stayed while the parties try to settle the case by alternative dispute resolution or other means. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Stay to allow for settlement of the case] (2) If all parties request a stay the proceedings shall be stayed for one month and the court shall notify the parties accordingly. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Stay to allow for settlement of the case] (3) If the court otherwise considers that such a stay would be appropriate, the court may direct that the proceedings, either in whole or in part, be stayed for one month, or for such other period as it considers appropriate. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Stay to allow for settlement of the case] (4) The court may extend the stay until such date or for such specified period as it considers appropriate. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Stay to allow for settlement of the case] (5) Where the court stays the proceedings under this rule, the claimant must tell the court if a settlement is reached. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Stay to allow for settlement of the case] (6) If the claimant does not tell the court by the end of the period of the stay that a settlement has been reached, the court shall give such directions as to the management of the case as it considers appropriate. ## Referral to the Mediation Service

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] 26.6. —(1) This rule applies to claims started in the County Court which would normally be allocated to the small claims track pursuant to rule 26.9. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] (2) This rule does not apply to—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] (a)road traffic accident, personal injury or housing disrepair claims; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] (b)any claim in which any party to the proceedings does not agree to referral to the Mediation Service. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] (3) In this rule, ‘the Mediation Service’ means the Small Claims Mediation Service operated by His Majesty’s Courts and Tribunals Service. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] (4) Where all parties indicate on their directions questionnaire that they agree to mediation, the claim shall be referred to the Mediation Service. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] (5) If a claim to which this rule applies is settled, the proceedings shall automatically be stayed with permission to apply for—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] (a)judgment for the unpaid balance of the outstanding sum of the settlement agreement; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] (b)the claim to be restored for hearing of the full amount claimed,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Referral to the Mediation Service] unless the parties have agreed that the claim is to be discontinued or dismissed. ## Allocation and assignment

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] 26.7. —(1) Subject to rule 26.8, the court shall allocate the claim to a track and, where applicable, assign it to a complexity band—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (a)after all parties have filed their directions questionnaires; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (b)when giving directions pursuant to rule 26.4(10),

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] unless it has stayed the proceedings under rule 26.5. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (2) If the court has stayed the proceedings under rule 26.5, it shall allocate the claim to a track and, where applicable, assign it to a complexity band at the end of the period of the stay. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (3) If—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (a)a claim is referred to the Mediation Service pursuant to rule 26.6; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (b)the court has not been notified in writing that a settlement has been agreed,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] the claim shall be allocated to a track and, where applicable, assigned to a complexity band in accordance with this rule no later than four weeks from the date on which the last directions questionnaire is filed. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (4) Before deciding the track to which to allocate or the complexity band to which to assign proceedings, or deciding whether to give directions for an allocation hearing or an assignment hearing to be fixed, the court may order a party to provide further information about his case. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (5) The court may hold an allocation hearing or an assignment hearing if it thinks it is necessary. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (6) If a party fails to file a directions questionnaire, the court may give any direction it considers appropriate. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (7) When, in a claim to which Section VI or Section VII of Part 45 applies, the court decides the track to which a claim should be allocated or the complexity band to which it should be assigned—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (a)it shall also consider whether it is in the interests of justice to order that rule 45.5(4) should apply to that claim; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > Allocation and assignment] (b)when considering whether it is in the interests of justice to make such an order, it shall have regard to whether the claim of each claimant arises from the same or substantially the same facts and gives rise to the same or substantially the same issues. ## Proceedings under Practice Direction 27B

## 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] (a)the parties have followed the Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims Below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] (b)proceedings have been started under Practice Direction 27B. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), where this rule applies, the claim shall be treated as allocated to the small claims track when it is issued and rules 26.4, 26.5 and 26.7 shall not apply. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] (3) Where in any claim started or continued under Practice Direction 27B—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] (a)the appropriate court form states that—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] (i)the amount claimed is more than £10,000; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] (ii)the claim for personal injury damages is more than £5,000; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] (b)rule 26.10 applies,

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.8. —(1) This rule applies where—] a court officer must refer the claim to a judge for allocation to a track and to give directions. ## Scope of each track

## 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (a)any claim for personal injuries where—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (i)the value of the claim is not more than £10,000; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (ii)the value of any claim for damages for personal injuries is not more than—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (aa)£5,000 in a claim for personal injuries arising from a road traffic accident, except as provided in sub-paragraph (bb);

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (bb)£1,000 in a claim for personal injuries arising from a road traffic accident, in any of the circumstances specified in rule 26.10; or

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (cc)£1,500 in any other claim for personal injuries. [PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (b)any claim which includes a claim by a tenant of residential premises against a landlord where—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (i)the tenant is seeking an order requiring the landlord to carry out repairs or other work to the premises (whether or not the tenant is also seeking some other remedy);

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (ii)the cost of the repairs or other work to the premises is estimated to be not more than £1,000; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (iii)the value of any other claim for damages is not more than £1,000; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (c)in relation to claims under the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016(1), any claim which includes a claim by a contract-holder of a dwelling against a landlord where—

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (i)the contract holder is seeking an order requiring the landlord to carry out repairs or other work to the dwelling (whether or not the contract-holder is also seeking some other remedy);

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (ii)the cost of repairs or other work to the dwelling is estimated to be not more than £1,000; and

[PART 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE > 26.9. —(1) The small claims track is the normal track for—] (iii)the value of any other claim for damages is not more than £1,000.
